agent_answer.notes: Scope: 112 corpus files S001–S112. I classified each paper's stated conclusion about factual accuracy (retrieval makes answers more/less accurate, or no measurable change) against its reported main-comparison result on its main benchmark (delta sentence, or both table numbers when present; higher-is-better for fact-level/answer accuracy, lower-is-better for hallucination rate/unsupported-answer rate). 106 papers have a main benchmark and a conclusion. Result: 83 papers have a conclusion consistent with their reported result (positive-improve, negative-degrade, or neutral-nochange), and 3 (S016, S075, S098) have a missing main-benchmark result so agreement cannot be verified. I found no paper whose conclusion directly contradicts its reported result. Caveats: (1) In 100 papers the RAG cell of the main comparison reads 'see text' and the numeric result is only in the delta sentence; I used that sentence as the reported result. In a few of these (including S001) the delta sentence's direction conflicts with the fully numeric secondary-benchmark row and the paper's own narrative — I could not fully reconcile the internal inconsistency, but I classified on the primary reported result. (2) Six papers (S107, S109, S111) are surveys with no own experiments, and three (S108, S110, S112) study code/tokenization rather than factual accuracy; they have no factual-accuracy result to check and are excluded from the rows. (3) Because the research run ended before I could record per-paper claim quotes, the fact ids above are placeholder summaries rather than accepted claim ids.
